root_cause.text: f2fs incorrectly created and destroyed inline xattr kmem_cache objects per-superblock in `f2fs_init_xattr_caches()`, even though the slab allocator can alias same-sized caches across mounts, causing multiple `sbi` instances to share one cache object while tracking it as separate per-sb state.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states caches like `f2fs_xattr_entry-7:3` and `f2fs_xattr_entry-7:7` with the same slab size “will only create one slab cache core structure,” “share the same structure and cache address,” and destroying one only decrements the refcount so recreating it later triggers “kmem_cache of name ... already exists”; correspondingly, the patch removes `inline_xattr_slab` from `struct f2fs_sb_info`, deletes per-sb init/destroy calls, and replaces them with a single global `inline_xattr_slab` created at filesystem init.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: f2fs incorrectly created and destroyed inline xattr kmem_cache objects per-superblock in `f2fs_init_xattr_caches()`, even though the slab allocator can alias same-sized caches across mounts, causing multiple `sbi` instances to share one cache object while tracking it as separate per-sb state.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The commit message states caches like `f2fs_xattr_entry-7:3` and `f2fs_xattr_entry-7:7` with the same slab size “will only create one slab cache core structure,” “share the same structure and cache address,” and destroying one only decrements the refcount so recreating it later triggers “kmem_cache of name ... already exists”; correspondingly, the patch removes `inline_xattr_slab` from `struct f2fs_sb_info`, deletes per-sb init/destroy calls, and replaces them with a single global `inline_xattr_slab` created at filesystem init.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove inline xattr slab cache fields from f2fs_sb_info as part of eliminating unused or relocated per-superblock slab state.
intent_record.what: Two fields were removed from struct f2fs_sb_info: the struct kmem_cache *inline_xattr_slab member and the unsigned int inline_xattr_slab_size member, along with their associated comments.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the f2fs superblock info structure no longer stores per-instance inline xattr slab cache metadata, which means that state must have been eliminated, moved elsewhere, or is no longer used; this reduces the structure's stored state rather than adding new checks or directly changing control flow in this hunk.

intent_record.intent_summary: Stop destroying xattr caches during f2fs_put_super() teardown to avoid incorrect or duplicate cleanup.
intent_record.what: The call to f2fs_destroy_xattr_caches(sbi) was removed from f2fs_put_super() immediately after f2fs_destroy_page_array_cache(sbi).
intent_record.how: At unmount/superblock teardown, the filesystem no longer destroys xattr caches from this code path, preventing that cleanup action from occurring here and likely avoiding an incorrect or duplicate cache teardown.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove xattr cache initialization from f2fs_fill_super() and adjust the error path to match the reduced setup sequence.
intent_record.what: The call to f2fs_init_xattr_caches(sbi) and its associated error handling branch were removed from f2fs_fill_super(), and the failure path for f2fs_init_page_array_cache(sbi) was changed from jumping to free_xattr_cache to jumping directly to free_percpu.
intent_record.how: At mount-time initialization, the filesystem no longer initializes per-sbi xattr slab caches in this function, and page array cache initialization failure now skips xattr-cache cleanup because that resource is no longer set up here.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove xattr cache destruction from this f2fs_fill_super error path to avoid incorrect cleanup during mount failure handling.
intent_record.what: The error-handling label and call that destroyed xattr caches were removed from f2fs_fill_super(): the free_xattr_cache label was deleted along with the f2fs_destroy_xattr_caches(sbi) call, causing control flow to fall directly from free_page_array_cache to free_percpu.
intent_record.how: On the corresponding failure path in superblock initialization, the function no longer attempts to destroy xattr caches before freeing percpu information, changing cleanup behavior so that xattr cache teardown is skipped in this path and avoiding a potentially invalid or redundant cleanup operation.

intent_record.intent_summary: Initialize the F2FS xattr cache during startup and clean it up on registration failure to avoid incomplete initialization and resource leaks.
intent_record.what: In init_f2fs_fs(), the direct call to register_filesystem(&f2fs_fs_type) after f2fs_create_casefold_cache() was replaced with a call to f2fs_init_xattr_cache(), followed by the register_filesystem(&f2fs_fs_type) call. A new error check and cleanup label were added so that if filesystem registration fails after xattr cache initialization, execution jumps to free_xattr_cache, which calls f2fs_destroy_xattr_cache() before continuing existing cleanup through free_casefold_cache and free_compress_cache.
intent_record.how: This change initializes the xattr cache during F2FS module startup before registering the filesystem, and ensures that the xattr cache is properly torn down if registration fails. It prevents leaked or partially initialized xattr cache state on initialization failure and makes xattr cache setup part of the normal startup sequence.

intent_record.intent_summary: Destroy the f2fs xattr cache during filesystem module exit to properly release teardown-time resources.
intent_record.what: In the f2fs module exit function exit_f2fs_fs(), a call to f2fs_destroy_xattr_cache() was added immediately after unregister_filesystem(&f2fs_fs_type) and before the existing cache and mempool destruction calls.
intent_record.how: At module unload or filesystem teardown time, the xattr cache is now explicitly destroyed, ensuring its allocated resources are released instead of being left behind after unregistering the filesystem.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use a shared global inline xattr slab cache and the default xattr slab size constant in `xattr_alloc()` instead of per-superblock slab fields.
intent_record.what: The patch adds a file-scope static `struct kmem_cache *inline_xattr_slab`, changes `xattr_alloc()` to test `size` against `DEFAULT_XATTR_SLAB_SIZE` instead of `sbi->inline_xattr_slab_size`, and switches the allocation call from `sbi->inline_xattr_slab` to the new global `inline_xattr_slab`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, inline xattr allocations are now selected using a fixed default slab size and served from a shared slab cache pointer rather than a per-superblock slab configuration, making the inline allocation path use the common cache consistently when the requested size matches the default inline xattr size.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix inline xattr deallocation to free objects from the correct inline_xattr_slab cache.
intent_record.what: The call to kmem_cache_free() in xattr_free() was changed to use inline_xattr_slab instead of sbi->inline_xattr_slab when is_inline is true.
intent_record.how: At runtime, inline extended attribute buffers are now freed through the slab cache referenced by the standalone inline_xattr_slab object rather than a field in the superblock info structure, aligning deallocation with the intended slab cache source and avoiding use of a removed or incorrect per-sbi slab pointer.

intent_record.intent_summary: Convert F2FS xattr slab cache management from per-superblock caches to a single global cache with fixed default sizing.
intent_record.what: The patch replaces the per-superblock xattr cache init/destroy functions with global versions: `f2fs_init_xattr_caches(struct f2fs_sb_info *sbi)` becomes `int __init f2fs_init_xattr_cache(void)` and `f2fs_destroy_xattr_caches(struct f2fs_sb_info *sbi)` becomes `void f2fs_destroy_xattr_cache(void)`. It removes code that derived a device-specific slab name from `sbi->sb->s_bdev->bd_dev`, computed `sbi->inline_xattr_slab_size` from the mount option, and stored the created cache in `sbi->inline_xattr_slab`. Instead it creates a single slab cache named `"f2fs_xattr_entry"` with `DEFAULT_XATTR_SLAB_SIZE`, stores it in `inline_xattr_slab`, and destroys that global cache in the teardown function.
intent_record.how: At runtime, xattr slab cache management changes from per-filesystem-instance allocation to a single global cache initialized at module/init time and destroyed globally. This removes device-specific slab naming and per-instance sizing based on `inline_xattr_size`, and makes cache creation succeed or fail based only on creation of the shared `inline_xattr_slab` object.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a macro for the default xattr slab size so code can consistently reference the computed inline xattr storage size including padding.
intent_record.what: A new macro definition, DEFAULT_XATTR_SLAB_SIZE, was added after DEFAULT_INLINE_XATTR_ADDRS; it computes a size as DEFAULT_INLINE_XATTR_ADDRS * sizeof(__le32) + XATTR_PADDING_SIZE.
intent_record.how: This introduces a reusable constant representing the default xattr slab allocation size, enabling code to use a single derived size value for default inline xattr storage including padding rather than recalculating it manually.

intent_record.intent_summary: Refactor the f2fs xattr cache API from per-superblock cache management to a global init/teardown interface and mark initialization as init-only.
intent_record.what: The xattr cache function declarations were changed from per-superblock interfaces taking a struct f2fs_sb_info * parameter (`f2fs_init_xattr_caches` and `f2fs_destroy_xattr_caches`) to global no-argument interfaces (`f2fs_init_xattr_cache` and `f2fs_destroy_xattr_cache`), and the init function was additionally annotated with `__init`.
intent_record.how: This changes the API from managing xattr caches on a per-filesystem-instance basis to managing a single cache lifecycle without requiring superblock context, and marks the initialization routine as init-only so its code can be discarded after system initialization.

intent_record.intent_summary: Update the no-xattr stub functions to match the new global xattr cache init/destroy interface and avoid build or linkage mismatches.
intent_record.what: The fallback inline stubs under the disabled xattr configuration were changed from `f2fs_init_xattr_caches(struct f2fs_sb_info *sbi)` and `f2fs_destroy_xattr_caches(struct f2fs_sb_info *sbi)` to `f2fs_init_xattr_cache(void)` and `f2fs_destroy_xattr_cache(void)`, removing the `struct f2fs_sb_info *sbi` parameter, changing the names from plural to singular, and adding the `__init` annotation to the init function.
intent_record.how: At runtime this does not alter the stub behavior itself, since the functions still immediately return success or do nothing, but it aligns the no-xattr configuration stubs with updated global cache initialization and teardown call sites that no longer operate per-superblock, preventing interface mismatches during compilation and ensuring the disabled-feature path builds and links correctly.

grouping_result.intent: Refactor the f2fs xattr cache API from per-superblock cache management to a global init/teardown interface and mark initialization as init-only.
Destroy the f2fs xattr cache during filesystem module exit to properly release teardown-time resources.
Fix inline xattr deallocation to free objects from the correct inline_xattr_slab cache.
Add a macro for the default xattr slab size so code can consistently reference the computed inline xattr storage size including padding.
Update the no-xattr stub functions to match the new global xattr cache init/destroy interface and avoid build or linkage mismatches.

consistency_review.core_intent: Refactor F2FS xattr cache management from per-superblock slab state and lifecycle hooks to a single global cache with global init/teardown and corresponding call-site cleanup.
Move F2FS xattr cache lifecycle management to the filesystem module init/exit paths so initialization and teardown happen in the correct global scope.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly replace the vulnerable per-superblock inline xattr kmem_cache lifecycle with a single global cache and remove per-sb tracking/init/teardown, which is exactly the root cause described.

The root cause is that xattr kmem_cache objects were managed per-superblock instead of globally, leading to shared slab caches being incorrectly tracked and destroyed multiple times. This group directly fixes that by moving xattr cache init/destroy from superblock mount/unmount paths to module-wide init/exit paths and removing per-superblock/error-path destruction.

The root cause is incorrect per-superblock handling of inline xattr slab caches, leading to shared cache objects being tracked separately. Fixing inline xattr deallocation to free from the correct inline_xattr_slab directly addresses the cache ownership/misassociation problem caused by that design.

The vulnerability centers on incorrect handling of inline xattr kmem_cache objects and their size/alignment. Adding a dedicated macro for the default xattr slab size directly relates to the same inline xattr slab/cache definition, ensuring consistent size computation including padding, which is part of the cache creation logic involved in the bug.

The stub updates are directly tied to the interface change from per-superblock xattr cache init/destroy to global cache management, which is the fix for the root cause. Although mechanical, they are necessitated by and aligned with the vulnerability-related change.

candidates.rationale: This is the core vulnerable operation: creating and storing an inline xattr kmem_cache per-superblock. Because same-sized slab caches can be aliased by the allocator, different sbi instances may end up sharing one underlying cache while each tracks it as private state.

This per-device naming setup reflects the flawed design of tying cache identity to each mounted superblock/device, even though slab cache aliasing ignores that intended per-sb ownership boundary for same-sized caches.

This confirms the code treats the cache pointer as a per-superblock resource whose lifecycle is independently managed, reinforcing the incorrect ownership model that leads to shared underlying cache objects across mounts.

Destroying the xattr cache during per-superblock teardown is directly dangerous once multiple sb instances may actually share the same aliased cache object. This embodies the incorrect per-sb destruction half of the bug.

This error-path cleanup likewise assumes the xattr cache is owned exclusively by one superblock and can be destroyed independently, which is invalid under slab aliasing and can trigger premature or duplicate destruction.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the core vulnerable creation site: it allocates and stores an inline xattr kmem_cache as if it were private to a single superblock. Because same-sized slab caches may be aliased by the allocator, multiple sbi instances can end up referring to the same underlying cache while each believes it owns it independently.

This per-superblock teardown destroys xattr caches under the assumption that the cache is exclusively owned by this sbi. If cache creation was aliased across mounts, this can destroy a cache still shared by other superblocks, causing premature or duplicate destruction.

This line supports the flawed per-device/per-superblock cache identity model. The design derives cache naming from the mounted device, but slab aliasing can ignore that intended ownership boundary for same-sized caches, contributing to the incorrect assumption of private per-sb caches.

This line reflects the incorrect ownership model by treating the cache pointer as a per-superblock resource whose existence and lifecycle are checked independently. That assumption is unsafe when the allocator may alias caches across different mounts.

It's been observed that kzalloc() on lookup_all_xattrs() are call
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit a999150f4fe3abbb7efd05411fd5b460be699943
Author: Chao Yu <chao@kernel.org>
Date:   Tue Feb 25 18:17:10 2020 +0800

    f2fs: use kmem_cache pool during inline xattr lookups
    
    It's been observed that kzalloc() on lookup_all_xattrs() are called millions
    of times on Android, quickly becoming the top abuser of slub memory allocator.
    
    Use a dedicated kmem cache pool for xattr lookups to mitigate this.
    
    Signed-off-by: Park Ju Hyung <qkrwngud825@gmail.com>
    Signed-o
bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it includes the exact cache init/destroy logic described in the root cause. The vulnerable construct is present in `f2fs_init_xattr_caches()` and `f2fs_destroy_xattr_caches()`: this commit creates a slab cache per-superblock using a generated name (`sprintf(slab_name, "f2fs_xattr_entry-%u:%u", MAJOR(dev), MINOR(dev));`) and stores it in `sbi->inline_xattr_slab`, then later destroys it with `kmem_cache_destroy(sbi->inline_xattr_slab);`. The root cause says f2fs incorrectly created/destroyed inline xattr `kmem_cache` objects per-superblock even though slab can alias same-sized caches across mounts, leading multiple `sbi` instances to share one cache while each tracks it as separate per-sb state. This code does exactly that: `sbi->inline_xattr_slab = f2fs_kmem_cache_create(slab_name, sbi->inline_xattr_slab_size);` creates a cache tied to each `sbi`, and all allocation/free paths (`kmem_cache_zalloc(sbi->inline_xattr_slab, ...)` and `kmem_cache_free(sbi->inline_xattr_slab, ...)`) rely on that per-sb pointer. There is no sign of the later fix, such as using a global/shared cache pool independent of superblock lifetime or avoiding per-sb create/destroy. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present and the fix is not.
